Consumer Non-Cyclicals: The Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector posted the second‑best median price gain among fifteen SGX sectors over the past month, outpacing the overall market. With ten listed companies, half recorded positive price changes in the same period, underscoring the breadth of the rally. The sector’s strong performance likely reflects robust domestic consumer confidence, a rebound in tourism spending, stable exchange rates, targeted government stimulus for retail and food services, and improved supply‑chain resilience that together buoy demand for everyday goods. These Singapore‑specific dynamics are uniquely supporting the health of the Consumer Non‑Cyclicals market.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector, comprising 84 listed companies, secured the 9th spot out of 15 in the median price‑change ranking over the past 30 days, outpacing the broader SGX market on that metric. Only 16 of the 84 constituents posted a positive price change, indicating that the sector’s edge stems from a relatively small group of strong performers rather than broad‑based gains. This outperformance likely reflects a surge in discretionary spending as tourism rebounds, consumer confidence rises, and disposable incomes improve, while tighter credit conditions and higher interest rates weigh on other sectors. Current market‑specific factors that can uniquely affect the sector’s health in Singapore include tourism recovery, consumer confidence levels, disposable‑income trends, import‑duty policies, currency fluctuations, and retail‑space cost pressures.
Transportation & Logistics: Out of fifteen SGX sectors, Transportation & Logistics ranked fourth for median price change over the past month, with three of its eight constituents posting gains. The sector’s median gain also outpaced the broader SGX average, suggesting stronger tailwinds. This likely reflects heightened regional freight demand, tighter port capacity, volatile fuel costs, new emissions regulations, and a surge in e‑commerce deliveries, all of which uniquely shape the Singapore logistics landscape. While a majority of firms (five) still recorded declines, the positive momentum among nearly 40% of the companies helped lift the sector’s overall performance.
Healthcare: Despite comprising 42 listed healthcare firms, the sector slipped to 14th out of 15 in the SGX ranking for median price change over the past 30 days, with its median lagging behind the overall market. Only ten companies posted a positive price move, underscoring the breadth of the decline. The underperformance may stem from tighter reimbursement policies, heightened regulatory scrutiny, and lingering supply‑chain pressures that have weighed on earnings expectations, while an ageing population and shifting investor sentiment toward biotech risk‑off play also dampen momentum. Additional Singapore‑specific factors such as recent changes to healthcare subsidies, currency volatility, and the rollout of new health‑tech initiatives further constrain the sector.
Properties & Real Estate: The Properties & Real Estate sector lagged behind the broader market, posting a median price decline that placed it 11th out of 15 sectors based on the last 30 days' median price changes. Out of the 53 listed companies, only 12 recorded a positive price movement, underscoring the breadth of the weakness. The under‑performance may stem from higher financing costs and tighter credit conditions that dampen buyer activity, while regulatory cooling measures and an oversupply of office and residential units weigh on investor sentiment. Additional market‑specific pressures include rising interest rates, construction cost inflation, shifting demographic demand, and tighter lending standards for developers. These factors together help explain why the sector’s median price change fell short of the SGX overall median.
Energy: The Energy sector, made up of 25 companies, ranked last (15 of 15) in the sector ranking based on median price changes over the past 30 days, and its median price change trails the overall SGX median. Only five of the 25 firms posted a positive price change during the same period, highlighting the breadth of the decline. This underperformance may stem from regional fuel price volatility, tighter emissions regulations, shifts in renewable subsidies, and supply‑chain disruptions affecting LNG imports, all of which uniquely pressure the Singapore Energy market. Together, the weak median movement and the limited number of gainers suggest a sector facing headwinds that are not yet reflected in broader market trends.
Utilities: Despite only two of its thirteen constituents posting gains, the Utilities sector secured the 8th spot out of 15 in the median price‑change ranking, outpacing the overall SGX median move. The sector’s modest outperformance likely reflects steady demand for electricity and water services, coupled with recent regulatory tariff adjustments and a favourable fuel‑price environment that have insulated earnings. At the same time, ongoing renewable‑energy integration targets and regional power‑grid constraints add pressure on margins. These market‑specific conditions help explain why the Utilities index moved higher even as most of its stocks fell.
Consumer Defensive: Among the fifteen SGX sectors, Consumer Defensive, with its 30 constituents, ranked sixth in median price change over the past 30 days, and its median gain surpassed the overall SGX median. Only four of the thirty firms posted a positive price move, indicating that the sector’s outperformance is driven by a few strong performers rather than broad‑based gains. The recent easing of input cost pressures and a rebound in local discretionary spending likely lifted those leaders, while the broader market remained subdued. Additional elements that can uniquely shape the health of the Consumer Defensive segment in Singapore include inflation trends, consumer confidence levels, tourism recovery, currency movements, and regulatory adjustments. Overall, the sector’s modest rank and limited number of positive contributors suggest a cautious outlook despite its short‑term edge over the index.
Financial Services: The Financial Services sector, with 29 listed firms, ranked fifth out of fifteen in median price change over the past 30 days, outpacing the broader SGX. Nine companies posted positive price moves, while the remainder recorded declines. The sector’s relative strength appears tied to a favorable interest‑rate outlook, resilient earnings from core banking activities, and recent regulatory easing that has boosted investor confidence. Additional market‑specific drivers include the stance of monetary policy, regional credit conditions, capital flow trends, and ongoing reforms to fintech licensing. Together, these factors have helped the Financial Services sector deliver stronger median gains than the overall market.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector posted a median price gain that outpaced the broader SGX, ranking seventh out of fifteen sectors based on the median price changes over the last 30 days. Out of the 15 listed companies, only four recorded a positive price change, while the remaining eleven fell, indicating that the sector’s edge stems from a few strong performers. This outperformance is likely driven by factors unique to Singapore’s market such as recent regulatory adjustments, accelerated telecom infrastructure upgrades, rising advertising spend, heightened consumer data demand, and intensified regional bandwidth competition.
Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector, made up of 36 companies, slipped to 10th place out of 15 in the median price‑change ranking over the past 30 days, with its median move lagging behind the overall SGX median. Only nine of the 36 constituents posted a positive price change, underscoring the breadth of the weakness. This underperformance likely reflects a combination of weaker global commodity prices, a slowdown in regional construction demand, tighter credit conditions, and heightened regulatory scrutiny on mining activities, all of which can uniquely pressure the sector within the Singapore market. Additional factors such as supply‑chain disruptions, fluctuations in the Singapore dollar, and shifts in environmental‑policy incentives further compound the sector’s challenges.
Infrastructures: Ranking first among fifteen SGX sectors, the Infrastructures segment posted the strongest median price gain over the past month, with five of its seven constituents posting positive returns. This outperformance relative to the broader market likely reflects heightened government capital projects and rising regional logistics demand, which have bolstered earnings expectations for infrastructure operators. Additionally, a supportive interest‑rate backdrop, ongoing regulatory approvals for new assets, and stable commodity price trends are conditions uniquely influencing the sector’s health on the Singapore index. With the majority of its stocks moving higher, the sector’s momentum suggests continued investor confidence.
REIT: The REIT sector, with 38 listed companies, secured the third spot out of fifteen in the sector ranking based on median price changes over the past 30 days, and it outperformed the broader SGX market during the same period. Twenty‑four of the REITs posted positive price moves, indicating broad-based strength across the group. This upside is likely driven by a combination of robust rental demand, stable income streams, and a favorable funding environment that has kept yields attractive for investors. Current market‑specific factors that can uniquely affect the health of Singapore REITs include interest‑rate trends, regulatory adjustments to land‑use policies, foreign investor sentiment, supply pipeline constraints, and overall macro‑economic growth outlook.
Industrials: The Industrials sector, made up of 126 companies, slipped to 12th place out of 15 in the 30‑day median price‑change ranking, with its median move lagging behind the SGX overall median. Only 25 of the 126 firms recorded a positive price change over the past month, underscoring the breadth of the weakness. This underperformance likely reflects lingering global supply‑chain bottlenecks, rising input and commodity costs, tighter financing conditions, regulatory tightening, and a slowdown in regional construction activity, all of which uniquely pressure Singapore’s industrial firms.
Technology: The Technology sector, comprising 57 listed companies, slipped to 13th place out of 15 in the sector ranking based on median price changes over the past 30 days, trailing the overall SGX median. Only 11 of those companies posted a positive price movement, underscoring the breadth of the decline. This underperformance may stem from a confluence of pressures such as lingering global chip supply constraints, heightened regional data‑privacy regulations, a slowdown in corporate IT spending, currency volatility, and intensified competition from neighbouring tech hubs. Together, these factors have weighed on investor sentiment and contributed to the sector’s weaker median return relative to the broader market.
